market_thesis.long_term: Years: three lines compound. First, compute and energy are now a single capital-allocation decision; capital is visibly rotating out of housing and rate-sensitive real assets (Real Estate -91, Utilities -87, mortgage rates at 2023 highs, Warsh-era rent 'doom loop' warnings) and into data centers and generation. Owning the fuel cycle, the grid and the merchant generator is the durable claim on AI, not owning the model. Second, agentic AI forces an identity, delegation and runtime-containment layer into existence — Nvidia explicitly shipping agent containment, cybersecurity topping all flow rankings — and security becomes a metered utility on every agent action, the most defensible annuity in the stack. Third, markets themselves are being unbundled: 24/7 tokenized equities, prediction markets at retail brokers, AI labs IPO-ing into public hands, private assets pushed toward retail late in a cycle. That structurally advantages venues, rails and brokers over asset gatherers, and it quietly transfers illiquidity and valuation risk to households. Demography is the slow fuse under all of it: Western populations start shrinking around 2029, which makes productivity-per-worker (automation, agents, healthspan) the only growth lever and public finances the permanent source of term premium.

shifts.shift: Electricity availability — not GPU supply — is the binding constraint on AI, pushing capital into behind-the-meter generation, gas/LNG contracted to data centres, demand flexibility and transmission EPC. Energy and compute are merging into one asset class.
Security — energy, supply-chain, digital and now agent containment — replaces convenience as the premium good; trust becomes a purchasable, non-discretionary budget line.

Consumers and enterprises buy AI as reclaimed time and delegated obligation, not as intelligence. Agentic tooling priced on outcomes wins; per-seat software without demonstrable labour substitution gets repriced down.

Housing need goes unmet and is adapted to rather than solved: renovation over relocation, smaller and manufactured formats, longer tenure, build-to-rent, multigenerational households; the first-time-buyer cohort shrinks permanently.
A structurally elevated term premium (5% risk-free, 5.44% 30-year, $365tn global debt) permanently impairs businesses whose moat was cheap capital and re-rates cash-generative owners of real assets.

Skilled physical labour with digital leverage — electricians, HVAC, pipeline and fab construction — is the true bottleneck to AI, grid and reshoring capex; wage premia persist and sustain contractor margins for years.

Memory and optics are the tightest, least-substitutable links in the AI chain and are insulated from a frontier-training pause because inference and edge deployment consume bits regardless of training cadence.

Financial intermediation becomes the growth industry of a high-rate, multi-venue, 24/7 world: tokenised settlement, retail democratization, multigenerational advice, custody and fraud protection. Status migrates from home equity to portfolio equity.
Inference migrates to the edge for cost, latency and privacy, shifting compute margin from centralized rental toward device silicon, memory and connectivity.
Health demand shifts from managed disease to restored function: procedures, robotic surgery and devices are actively shopped by an aging population, alongside pharmacological metabolic management.
